listing.name: OpenArena
listing.summary: Play OpenArena’s standalone maps and modes with the game data in its own release.

restrictions.explanation: Use the complete publisher ZIP or the Linux distribution package. These players are installed and updated outside Portcove.

steps.title: Use the complete Windows release
steps.instruction: Extract openarena-0.8.8.zip into a dedicated folder and keep baseoa and missionpack beside openarena.exe. The full release includes the base game and both patches. The Windows player is 32-bit and needs Windows support for 32-bit applications. Start openarena.exe from that folder.

steps.title: Choose the upstream Linux player
steps.instruction: On Debian or Ubuntu, install openarena with your package manager and let it install the engine and map packages. For the older publisher ZIP, extract openarena-0.8.8.zip and run ./openarena.x86_64 from the openarena-0.8.8 folder with baseoa and missionpack beside it. That binary needs SDL 1.2, Vorbis and a working OpenGL driver.

steps.title: Back up your OpenArena profile
steps.instruction: Close the game and copy %APPDATA%/OpenArena on Windows or ~/.openarena on Linux, including baseoa/q3config.cfg, custom maps, demos and mods. Keep any custom content you added to the installation separately before replacing it.

warnings: Use OpenArena’s own data and add-ons. If you join a server, use the game version and assets the server expects.

references.title: Use the separate Android port
references.instruction: The separately maintained PlayFDroid OpenArena Android release has touchscreen controls and downloads the official game data into app-specific storage on first launch. Follow its release and installation instructions. Desktop profile folders do not apply to that app.

references.title: Check Mac compatibility
references.instruction: The official 0.8.8 ZIP contains legacy 32-bit Intel and PowerPC Mac binaries. Use those only with a matching legacy Mac environment. Current Intel and Apple Silicon Macs need a separately built player.
